knowledge:
- key_parameters: n=Number of top commonly expressed genes to select in common_genes (e.g., n = 100) ;; thresh=Proportion threshold in add_snps to filter out SNPs with no reads in less than 'thresh' proportion of cells (e.g., thresh = 0.95) ;; train_cells=Logical vector in reassign_centroid specifying which cells to use for training (high-confidence singlets) ;; predict_cells=Logical vector in reassign_centroid specifying which cells to predict ;; min_cells=Minimum number of cells required for a group to be considered in reassign_centroid (e.g., min_cells = 5) ;; assay=Name of the alternative experiment assay containing HTO counts in high_conf_calls (default is "HTO")
- alternatives: Standalone cell hashing methods (e.g., Seurat HTODemux, demuxmix, BFF, cellhashR, CiteFuse) should be preferred when SNP data is unavailable or groups are not genetically distinct ;; Genotype-based demultiplexing (e.g., demuxlet) should be preferred when high-quality reference genotype information for each group is already available ;; Unsupervised SNP-based demultiplexing (e.g., Souporcell, Vireo) should be preferred when cell hashing data is unavailable but groups are genetically distinct, though they may struggle with low-abundance groups
- when_to_use: Use when multiplexing genetically distinct samples in scRNA-seq with cell hashing (HTO/LMO) tags, especially when some cells cannot be confidently assigned by cell hashing alone due to poor tagging quality, but have high-quality RNA
- pitfalls: Ensure the genome assembly version of the VCF file and the EnsDb object are compatible (e.g., both hg38 or hg19) ;; Variant calling (generating the SNP matrix) is not performed within the package; users must run external tools like VarTrix on their BAM files using the subsetted VCF ;; Low-quality cells (low library size or high mitochondrial percentage) should be filtered out prior to running the workflow

workflows.name: supervised_demultiplexing_hashing_snps
workflows.intent: Demultiplex multiplexed scRNA-seq cells by training a classifier on high-confidence cell hashing assignments and predicting unassigned cells using SNP profiles.
input: multiplexed_scrnaseq_sce (SingleCellExperiment object containing RNA counts and HTO/LMO counts as an alternative experiment)
commonvariants_1kgenomes_subset (VCF file containing common genetic variants, e.g., from 1000 Genomes)
vartrix_consensus_snps (Matrix of SNP calls per cell generated externally by VarTrix)
EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86 (Ensembl annotation database object matching the reference genome)
workflows.stages: 1. Identify top commonly expressed genes in the scRNA-seq data using common_genes ;; 2. Subset the common variants VCF file to those within the top expressed genes using subset_vcf ;; 3. Identify high-confidence cell hashing assignments using high_conf_calls ;; 4. Add the externally generated VarTrix SNP matrix to the SingleCellExperiment object using add_snps ;; 5. Reassign low-confidence or unassigned cells to their genetic groups using reassign_centroid
workflows.code:
top_genes <- common_genes(sce = multiplexed_scrnaseq_sce, n = 100)
ensdb <- EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86::EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86
new_vcf <- subset_vcf(commonvariants_1kgenomes_subset, top_genes = top_genes, ensdb)
multiplexed_scrnaseq_sce <- high_conf_calls(multiplexed_scrnaseq_sce)
multiplexed_scrnaseq_sce <- add_snps(multiplexed_scrnaseq_sce, vartrix_consensus_snps, thresh = 0.95)
set.seed(1)
multiplexed_scrnaseq_sce$labels<-as.character(multiplexed_scrnaseq_sce$labels)
multiplexed_scrnaseq_sce$knn <- reassign_centroid(multiplexed_scrnaseq_sce,
    train_cells = multiplexed_scrnaseq_sce$train,
    predict_cells = multiplexed_scrnaseq_sce$predict,
    min_cells = 5
)
